messages:
maria gonzalez: FYI I'm kicking off a small rewrite of our internal incident comms templates — trying to make the language clearer for on-call handoffs and customer status updates. want quick feedback on tone/placeholders.

jon r: thanks. skimmed the draft in the doc, will drop comments. main ask: separate "what we know" vs "what we're doing" and use neutral language for impact. avoid absolutes like 'all customers' unless verified.

incident-bot: [pagerduty] P1 alert acknowledged by @maria gonzalez — latency spike on inference-host-3. Pager: 2 alerts in last 3m.

maria gonzalez: ^ attaching that to this thread because template needs to include a short live-mitigation section for on-call notes.

kevin wu: quick thought — in the status page template we should include a "possible customer impact" field with levels: none/minor/major/unknown, and a one-line recommended customer-facing sentence. keeps comms consistent.

sara-l: Agree. And let's standardize placeholders: 
- {INCIDENT_ID} 
- {AFFECTED_SERVICE} 
- {START_TIME} 
- {ESTIMATED_RESTORE} (optional) 
- {WORKAROUND} (if any) 
- {NEXT_UPDATE}
Make sure examples show how to fill those.

emily: Tone note: customers prefer "we're investigating" to "we're working on it" initially? I think "investigating" sets expectation better. Also include a short line about "no known data loss" unless confirmed.

jon r: +1. Also include a short internal-only section header in templates like "On-call notes (internal)" that includes runbook links and safe copy for execs.

maria gonzalez: OK I'm pasting a status page draft for a latency incident — please read and give inline suggestions. This is the single-string body we'll use for status pages and customer-notif variants.

maria gonzalez: STATUS PAGE DRAFT: 

{INCIDENT_ID}: Elevated latency observed on {AFFECTED_SERVICE} 
Start: {START_TIME} UTC

What we know:
- We are observing increased 95th/99th percentile latency for inference requests routed to inference-host-3.
- Error rates are not elevated at this time.
- Root cause is under investigation.

What we're doing (mitigation):
- On-call is actively investigating instance telemetry and control-plane routing.
- Increasing routing weight away from inference-host-3 as a measure to reduce customer impact.
- If applicable, we will scale a replacement pool for affected capacity.

Customer impact:
- Possible increased latency for a subset of hosted API requests in region us-west-2. Impact level: minor/major/unknown (fill as appropriate).
- No evidence of data corruption or loss at this time.

Workaround (if any):
- Retry with exponential backoff. Consider using pinned model variants that are served from alternative pools.

Next update: {NEXT_UPDATE} (target within 15 minutes)

Communication guidance (internal):
- Use neutral, factual language. avoid speculation.
- Do not promise recovery timelines unless ops confirms.
- If asked, provide a short "customer-facing" sentence only, e.g. "We're seeing elevated latency in us-west-2 affecting a subset of requests; our team is investigating and will provide updates."

Standard placeholders and examples:
- {INCIDENT_ID}: IN-1862
- {AFFECTED_SERVICE}: Redwood inference API (text generation)
- {START_TIME}: 2026-03-14 21:02:00 UTC
- {NEXT_UPDATE}: 21:17 UTC

maria gonzalez: thoughts?

jon r: looks good. Suggest adding a short "who's on it" line in internal comms that lists primary responder + secondary so handoffs are explicit. e.g., "Primary: @maria gonzalez, Secondary: @jon r".

kevin wu: Also add a checkbox at the end for "status page published" + "customer emails sent" + "exec notified" so ops-scribe can mark what happened during the incident.

sara-l: For wording library: include alternatives for common sentences so responders can pick tone: 
- Neutral: "We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests."
- Reassuring: "We are actively mitigating an issue that may cause higher latency for some requests; there is no evidence of data loss."
- Concise (for high-volume updates): "Investigating latency in us-west-2 — more updates soon."

emily: Good idea to include 'DO NOTs' too: 
- DO NOT say "fixed" until verified for all affected variants. 
- DO NOT assign blame to teams or vendors in customer messages. 
- DO NOT include internal metrics like raw p95/p99 numbers unless you know customers want that.

incident-bot: [incident-note] Handoff requested: primary acknowledged but needs 30m break. @jon r requested as secondary.

jon r: I'm taking the secondary. planning to join in 5 to do handoff.

maria gonzalez: handoff notes (internal): 
- Current suspicion: degraded NVLink saturation on inference-host-3 causing slow kernel dispatch.
- Logs to check: /var/log/inference/runtime.log, kernel scheduler QPS, network rx/tx.
- Immediate mitigation done: routing weight reduced to 10% for host-3.
- Next steps: scale replacement pool + run a drain on host-3 once traffic is low.

ops-scribe: I'll maintain the checklist below and mark items as we go. copying into incident timeline.

ops-scribe: CHECKLIST (internal) — please update with initials when complete:
- [ ] Status page draft created 
- [ ] Status page published 
- [ ] Customer email drafted 
- [ ] Customer email sent 
- [ ] Exec summary prepared 
- [ ] Postmortem scheduled

kevin wu: For customer email template, we should include templated subject lines depending on impact: 
- Minor: "Brief service disruption affecting some requests in us-west-2"
- Major: "Service disruption impacting Redwood inference API in us-west-2"

maria gonzalez: CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE (concise):
Subject: {INCIDENT_ID} — {AFFECTED_SERVICE} latency in {REGION}
Body:
Hi,

We are investigating elevated latency for a subset of requests to {AFFECTED_SERVICE} in {REGION}. Our team has identified affected hosts and is taking steps to mitigate customer impact. At this time, we have no evidence of data loss.

What we're doing:
- Reducing traffic to affected hosts
- Scaling replacement capacity

We will provide our next update by {NEXT_UPDATE}.

If you have critical SLA concerns, reply to this message or contact support.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations

maria gonzalez: ok final ask: can we maintain a mini-phrase library for different contexts (status page vs email vs internal slack) so responders don't have to reword each time. I can start a small doc.

jon r: awesome. I'll add short pre-approved lines for exec comms — one paragraph, high level, include potential business impact if known.

sara-l: I'll make a quick PR to the template repo to add these placeholders and the do/don't list.

emily: and I'll coordinate with support for the customer email distribution list + any legal/compliance approvals for wording.

ops-scribe: Noted. I'll take care of the checklist updates in the incident timeline and publish the status page once the primary confirms.

maria gonzalez: thanks everyone. wrapping up: main changes we'll land:
- explicit "who's on it" in internal templates
- standardized placeholders + examples
- a short wording library with 3 tones + DO/DO NOT list
- add checklist fields for notification artifacts

maria gonzalez: leaving this thread open for pair review. if nobody objects I'll merge the template updates after lunch. :thumbsup:

jon r: lgtm

kevin wu: lgtm

sara-l: +1

incident-bot: [incident-resolved] Pager duty alert resolved for IN-1862 — monitoring.

maria gonzalez: incident resolved. publishing final status and post-incident steps in the timeline.

ops-scribe: final checklist update: 
- [x] Status page draft created 
- [x] Status page published 
- [x] Customer email drafted 
- [x] Customer email sent 
- [x] Exec summary prepared 
- [ ] Postmortem scheduled (I'll create a calendar invite)

maria gonzalez: thanks all. I'll follow up with a draft postmortem template referencing wording choices.

ops-scribe: noted — closing thread once postmortem invite is sent.
